title: Hamilton County to conclude curbside flood debris collection on September 3
text:
Hamilton County to conclude curbside flood debris collection on September 3
Hamilton County will end its curbside flood debris collection program on Thursday, September 3, as the county moves from widespread debris removal to long-term recovery efforts, according to a Sept. 2 announcement.
Officials said there has been a significant decrease in the amount of material being placed at the curb in neighborhoods affected by recent flooding. Residents who still have debris are instructed to place it at the curb on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday where crews can safely access it, and call the Flood Hotline at 317-645-3261 to have their address added to the final pickup list.
After the holiday weekend, crews will conduct one last sweep through impacted areas to collect any remaining flood debris. This effort will mark the official conclusion of Hamilton County’s special flood debris collection program. Following this period, residents must use regular trash services or other standard disposal methods for any additional waste.
Since collections began on August 24, crews have removed about 2,749 cubic yards of construction and demolition materials from flooded neighborhoods. In addition, approximately 18,608 pounds of household hazardous waste has been collected and properly disposed of.
The county contracted CrowderGulf for curbside collection operations and Tidal Basin Group for monitoring and documenting the process. Officials said that thorough documentation is necessary, as Hamilton County seeks reimbursement through the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Public Assistance Program.
